Color field guide

Better color decisions, without the theory lecture.

Short, practical notes for moving from an attractive combination to a palette that actually works.

01 · Roles

Five colors, five jobs.

A useful palette separates background, surface, primary, accent, and text. The colors can change; the responsibilities stay clear.

Test the roles →
02 · Contrast

Harmony is not readability.

Two colors can feel perfect together and still fail as text and background. Context and contrast belong in the same decision.

Find a direction →
03 · Images

Dominant is not always important.

A small, vivid detail may carry more visual meaning than a large neutral area. Compare the observed, focused, and applied readings.

Read an image →
Useful questions

Things worth asking before you commit.

Why does ColorVerse use five colors?+

Five is enough to separate surfaces, hierarchy, emphasis, and readable text without turning the palette into an inventory.

Should every color come directly from the source image?+

No. Observed colors describe the image; applied colors may adjust lightness and contrast so the system works in a real interface or layout.

Can I choose more than one color on the globe?+

Yes. Choose up to five. If you choose fewer, ColorVerse generates supporting roles around your selection.

What happens to an image I upload?+

Image extraction runs locally in your browser. The image is not uploaded or published unless a future community sharing flow asks for separate, explicit permission.

Can two people use the same palette?+

Yes. Color combinations are starting material. The distinctive value usually comes from how they are applied, named, composed, and connected to a project.
